cues.en: I'm an entertainment channel. I shoot my vlog on an Apple watch. I do the chroma key by pressing a button in my app labeled background boo. So don't come to me with whack questions like, how come in the digital age, we now mostly use green screen instead of blue? I mean, to to understand that, you would first...... To ask yourself a simple question, whom is this technology for? And the answer almost always is apes. Descendants of apes whose retinas evolved much more sensitivity to luminance than to color. Being able to detect a lion leaping at your face takes precedence over being able to admire its majestic mane. And what little color sensitivity our redness have is extremely biased toward green, probably because of all the green. So when devising a way to distribute red, green, and blue wavelengths of light onto a limited number of elements on a photo sensor array, a scientist named Bryce Bayer invented and swiftly patented the Bayer filter, a recursive pattern that dedicates half the sensors to green and splits the other half between red and blue. Why bother imitating reality when you can simply imitate an ape's perception of reality at one third the cost? A version of the Bayer filter is present in every camera using a CMOS chip from the phone in your pocket to the red epic stereo rigs that filmed all four hundred and seventy four excruciating minutes of the Hobbit trilogy. Each gives us a decent red channel, an abysmally noisy blue channel, and a crisp clean green channel with effectively double the resolution,
cues.zh: 我可是个娱乐频道。我用Apple Watch拍vlog。抠像就是按一下我app里那个叫"背景拜拜"的按钮。所以别拿这种莫名其妙的问题来问我，比如为什么数字时代我们大多用绿幕而不是蓝幕？我是说，要理解这个，你得先……先问自己一个简单的问题：这技术是给谁用的？答案几乎永远是：猿类。猿的后代，视网膜对亮度的敏感度远高于对颜色的敏感度。能发现扑向你的狮子，比欣赏它威武的鬃毛重要得多。而我们视网膜那点可怜的色彩敏感度还极度偏向绿色，大概是因为到处都是绿色吧。所以在想办法把红、绿、蓝三种波长分配到感光阵列有限数量的元件上时，一位叫Bryce Bayer的科学家发明并迅速申请了专利，这就是拜耳滤镜，一种递归图案，把一半传感器分给绿色，另一半分给红蓝。既然能花三分之一的成本模仿猿对现实的感知，何必费劲模仿现实本身呢？每台用CMOS芯片的相机里都有拜耳滤镜的某个版本，从你口袋里的手机，到拍下《霍比特人》三部曲那折磨人的四百七十四分钟的RED Epic Stereoscopic支架。它给我们一个还行的红色通道、一个噪点惨不忍睹的蓝色通道，还有一个清晰干净的绿色通道，有效分辨率直接翻倍，

cues.en: We can dedicate the first instance of the effect to broadly cut away all parts of the background that must be transparent and fill all parts of the foreground that must be opaque, then inflate the border. This way, a second instance of the effect no longer needs to deal with the image as a whole. We've limited its influence to the area immediately around the edge, so we're free to adjust its settings more finely. And if that doesn't do it, we can keep adding iterations until it's perfect. This iterative approach works for more than just green screen. We see it in art, in construction, in education.
cues.zh: 我们可以把效果的第一个实例专门用于大致去除背景中所有必须透明的部分，填充前景中所有必须不透明的部分，然后膨胀边缘。这样，效果的第二个实例就不再需要处理整张图像。我们已经把它的影响限制在边缘周围的区域，所以可以更精细地调整它的设置。如果这样还不够，我们可以继续增加迭代，直到完美。这种迭代方法不只适用于绿幕。我们在艺术、建筑、教育中都能看到它。

cues.zh: 现在，我可能只是个简单的火箭工程师，

cues.en: but this inanimate object was able to teach me something to to make me smarter yet again.
cues.zh: 但这个无生命的物体却能教会我一些东西，让我再次变得更聪明。

cues.en: Maybe this is not so bad.

I totally understand how it works and I'm on there all the time. One important thing I wanna ask you to do that no one has ever asked you before, become my patron on Patreon. I have seven reward tiers and I can barely keep up. And of course, badger your parents until they, say it with me, buy that merch. And don't forget my new hit single Troll Face Girl drops tomorrow.
cues.zh: 我敢说，改变世界。不。不。我是有商业可行性的。听着，在Instagram和Twitter上关注我。在Facebook、Snapchat上赞我的页面。我完全明白它是怎么运作的，我一直都在上面。有一件重要的事我想请你做，以前从没人问过你，成为我Patreon上的赞助人。我有七个奖励等级，我几乎忙不过来。当然，缠着你的父母直到他们，跟我一起说，买那个周边商品。别忘了我的新热门单曲《Troll Face Girl》明天发布。
